Britannica Editors History Britannica AI Ask Anything Table of Contents Table of Contents Ask Anything transcendental number, number that is not algebraic, in the sense that it is not the solution of an algebraic equation with rational-number coefficients. Transcendental numbers are irrational, but not all irrational numbers are transcendental. For example, x2 – 2 = 0 has the solutions x = ±Square root of√2; thus, Square root of√2, an irrational number, is an algebraic number and not transcendental. Nearly all real and complex numbers are transcendental, but very few numbers have been proven to be transcendental. The numbers e and π are transcendental numbers.
